                                    PROJECT NO. 58481


RULEMAKING TO INPLEMENT                        §      PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION                     §
STANDARDS UNDER PURA § 37.0561                 §                     OF TEXAS



                           COMMENTS OF
      NIGHTPEAK ENERGY LLC ON STAFF’S PROPOSAL FOR PUBLICATION
                        OF NEW 16 TAC §25.194

Nightpeak Energy LLC (“Nightpeak”) files these comments on the Commission Staff’s Proposal
for Publication (“Proposal”) regarding new Large Load Interconnection Standards for large loads
interconnecting into the ERCOT Transmission Grid. While Nightpeak understands and supports
the motives behind the proposed changes, which includes among other things, shrinking the large
load interconnection queue and weeding out speculative projects, we believe that this Proposal
will cause many high-quality data center projects to become unviable and/or postponed. It has
been demonstrated that the economic benefits of completed data center projects are material for
the State, Counties, and Local Municipalities.

Nightpeak is a power plant owner operator and early-stage data center developer. We locate the
data centers we develop adjacent or near to our power plants to ensure that data centers don’t
negatively impact local grid reliability and have access to dispatchable power. We are currently
actively developing a two-phase data center near our Bulldog power plant near Sweeny While
these comments are primarily focused on the Proposal, it is our understanding that this
rulemaking will set new standards which will be incorporated into the new ERCOT Batch Study
Protocols process currently underway. Therefore, our comments may be applicable to both this
Proposal and the new ERCOT Batch Study Process. Our comments will focus on these issues –

   1) The proposed Interconnection Agreement in this Proposal must contain the same
      language on financial commitment as the Order in Project No. 58480.

   2) The $100,000/MW non-refundable security deposit is too high.

   3) Large load projects that are included in the 2026 Regional Transmission Plan (RTP)
      should automatically be included in the ERCOT Batch Zero Studies.




                                               1
                                           COMMENTS
      1. The proposed Interconnection Agreement financial commitment language in this
         Proposal must contain the same language as the financial commitment requirement
         for inclusion into the 2026 RTP from the Order in Project No. 58480.

The financial commitment language from the 58480 Order for the criteria for inclusion into the
2026 RTP states –

“A large load customer must demonstrate financial commitment by means of one of the
following:
       (A) posting of security in the amount of $100,000 per MW of contracted peak demand;
       (B) posting of financial security to the DSP or TSP in an amount equal to the DSP and
       TSP's expected costs for equipment with a lead time of at least six months and services
       necessary to interconnect the large load; or
       (C) payment of contribution in aid of construction (CIAC) in an amount that is equal to
       the DSP and TSP's expected costs to interconnect the large load customer that are directly
       attributable to interconnecting the large load customer. The costs for CIAC must be
       remitted through a direct cash payment and include the following:
               (i) costs associated with one or more new transmission lines built to interconnect
               the large load customer to the existing transmission network, including substation
               upgrades necessary to interconnect the new large load customer; and
               (ii) costs associated with system upgrades that would not be required but for the
               interconnecting large load customer.” 1

In this Proposal, there is no option to pay a security deposit as it is a direct requirement of an
Interconnection Agreement – “Non-refundable interconnection fee”. A large load customer must
pay an interconnection fee in the amount of $100,000 per MW of contracted peak demand. An
interconnection fee under this subsection is non-refundable. 2 This could cost a data center
developer of an average 600 MW project to have to pay a minimum of $60,000,000 to stay in the
queue.

In the Proposal the Interconnection Agreement will be required to include the interconnection fee
plus posting financial security for the TSP’s cost of equipment necessary to interconnect a large
load customer plus the CIAC plus financial security for cost of system upgrades. This will have
the unintended effect of killing otherwise viable projects and the economic benefits that come
with the projects. While Nightpeak agrees that projects that are not as far along in the
interconnection process should be required to pay a large security deposit, the projects that have
advanced in the interconnection process are more viable and less speculative projects.

      2. The $100,000/MW non-refundable security deposit is too high.

Nightpeak believes that a much lower per MW amount will still have the same effect on thinning
out the large load interconnection queue that the proposed $100k per MW will have. Nightpeak

1
    Pg 92, ORDER ADOPTING NEW 16 TAC §25.370 Project 58480
2
    Pg 22, Staff Recommended Proposal for Publication

                                                             2
 recommends a 50% refundable $25,000 per MW interconnection fee. At this level, developers
who wish to submit large load interconnection applications will still demonstrate meaningful
access to capital and have sufficient “skin in the game” to only select likely viable
interconnections.

The proposed $100k/MW is an extremely high fee that will have the likely effect of directing
credible developers to locate sites outside of Texas, which may impact Texas economic
development. This is partially because there are additional costs to this fee, including the cost of
capital, which makes it far more expensive. For example, for a conventional developer with a
cost of capital of 15%, a $100,000 per MW fee over a four-year development and construction
cycle would add an additional 52% to the cost of the fee, which would imply a year-four
interconnection fee of $152,088 per MW. For a 600 MW project, that would equate to an
additional $31,252,800 of cost before the data center has an opportunity to earn revenue.

  3. Large load projects that are included in the 2026 Regional Transmission Plan (RTP)
     should automatically be included in the ERCOT Batch Zero Studies and not be
     required to pay an Interconnection Fee

In order to be included in the 2026 RTP a Large Load project has to 1) have all TSP
interconnection studies competed and approved by ERCOT, 2) Must have an executed Full
Interconnection Agreement, 3) Security posted that is equal to the cost of building the
interconnection facility and provide site control as per Order 58480. Large load projects which
are included and studied as part of the 2026 RTP are more viable projects. Based on these facts,
projects in the 2026 RTP should automatically be included in the ERCOT Batch Zero Studies.

Projects that demonstrate the above should not be subject to the Interconnection Fee. That is
because the issuance of interconnection Notice to Proceed (NTP), and thus capital at risk through
the posting of security, is predicated on a project’s perceived maturity and the ability for a project
sponsor and lenders to continue to fund it. Projects at this stage have most likely already received
Final Investment Decision and/or unrestricted NTP based on a specific project budget and
economics, which are now materially at risk due to a regulatory change which acts as a major
new tax. This surprise tax-like Interconnection Fee will impact projects’ viability and would have
likely influenced the sponsor’s decision to move forward and commit to continued construction.
Without an exception to the Interconnection Fee, it is possible that already under construction
projects would be halted and abandoned.

                                          CONCLUSION

In conclusion, the Proposal’s language for financial security for an interconnection fee should be
consistent with the financial security to enter the 2026 RTP from Order 58480. A “one of the
following” instead of “all of the above” approach which will be appropriately matched with the
progress of a project in the interconnection process. If an Interconnection Fee is required,
Nightpeak recommends a $25,000 per MW fee is appropriate and will have the effect of
cancelling non-viable projects. Also, if a large load gets included in the 2026 RTP, then that
project has an increased viability and locked project budget and economics and should be


                                                  3
 automatically included in the ERCOT Batch Zero and should not have to pay the interconnection
fee.

                                                         Respectfully Submitted,

/s/ Greg Blue___________________
Greg Blue
Director of Development
Nightpeak Energy LLC
3821 Arlington Ave
Tyler TX 75701
(925) 323-3612
Gblue@nightpeak.energy

March 11, 2026
